| [QUESTION-080](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-080.md) | When a trained network's parameters keep moving after its loss has converged, what about the network stays fixed, and is the last-layer geometry of neural collapse among the things that do? | The record holds two pictures of the end of training. In one, the last layer converges to a fixed geometry through the terminal phase ([THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), neural collapse). In the other, the parameters never stop: they sample a stationary distribution at constant speed ([THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)). The two may describe different regimes. The terminal phase of neural collapse is cross-entropy training past zero error, with no finite minimum, while the limiting dynamics assume a quadratic minimum. Nothing in the record relates them. Drawn by the assistant from the reading of Kunin et al., and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) | When the relative scale of a network's layers sets its learning regime under gradient flow, does that regime survive SGD, whose minibatch noise drives the relative scale toward balance, and on what timescale compared with learning? | Two readings meet here. Under gradient flow, the relative scale of adjacent layers is conserved and sets whether learning is rich or lazy ([THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md), Dominé et al.). Under SGD, that scale is not conserved: minibatch noise drives it toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances, at a rate set by η/S ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md), Ziyin et al.). If the drift is fast compared with learning, an unbalanced start chosen to be lazy would drift toward balance and richness. If it is slow, the regime set at initialization stands. Neither paper addresses the other. Drawn by the assistant from reading both, and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
